comment.body:
Unfortunately, https://v18.next.forgejo.org/franke/forgejo-runner-premature-success-repro/src/commit/9d2c3c495e41bb0e6d4aaa111447e793de050ad1/exec_stream_closed_test.go doesn't reproduce the problem, because it mocks the Docker API in Go.

This workflow should do it:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: debian
    steps:
      - run: |
          apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3
      - run: |
          import os
          import time
          import sys
        
          os.close(sys.stdout.fileno())
          
          time.sleep(10)
        shell:
          python3
```

The step is marked as succeeded after 0s instead of 10s.

https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c07a9b3669dc64d498273d47ce0e6974718792f1/act/container/docker/run.go#L766

continues until it encounters an EOF. Afterwards, Docker's `execInspect` is invoked.

https://code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner/src/commit/c07a9b3669dc64d498273d47ce0e6974718792f1/act/container/docker/run.go#L771

Unfortunately, it doesn't seem to help us much. It immediately returns `Running` as `false`, and the exit code is always 0, even if there's none, because Go.

The same script invoked using `podman exec <container> python3 test.py` takes ~10s.

Either, the workflow doesn't reproduce the problem perfectly, or `podman exec` does something differently. If somebody has any ideas, please let me know.
